findings.failure_scenario: Every one of the 8 Python resources runs `python -m alembic upgrade head` unconditionally on EVERY boot (TASK_MODE branch: entrypoint.sh:10; web mode: entrypoint.sh:47) — not just on deploy, but on every scheduled cron tick, since Railway starts a fresh container per cron invocation. A push to main that includes a migration causes the FIRST container (of any of the 9 resources) to boot on the new image to advance alembic_version to the new revision. Any OTHER resource that has not yet received the new image — because Railway's redeploy of 9 separate resources from one push is 'near-simultaneous', not atomic — will, on its next boot (its own redeploy completing late, or an unrelated crash-restart, or simply its cron schedule firing mid-rollout), run `alembic upgrade head` against a DB already at a revision its own local alembic/versions/ directory has never heard of. Alembic cannot resolve that revision and raises (observed live, per the requesting agent's direct read of Railway logs today): "Can't locate revision identified by '007' / FAILED / Stopping Container". The container exits non-zero and Railway's on_failure restart policy (railway.toml:7) retries it — which fails identically until that resource's own redeploy finishes and it receives the migration file. This is corroborated inside the repo by docs/DECISIONS-PENDING.md:49-51, which logs the matching successful half of the same 2026-08-13 event ('Boot log 2026-08-13 21:00 UTC: Running upgrade 006 -> 007') for whichever container won the race, and by alembic/versions/003_placeholder.py:6-10, an earlier, differently-caused instance of the same root problem (alembic_version diverged from what a given codebase snapshot's migration files can resolve).

gate.assert: Requested by the task: propose a real fix, not just document the bug. Three concrete options, none implemented in this repo today (evidence: entrypoint.sh has no locking, no leader-election, and no separate migration phase; railway.toml has no pre-deploy/release-phase command field): (1) Move `alembic upgrade head` out of every service's boot path into exactly one dedicated one-shot migration job that all 9 resources' deploys wait on before starting — this is the only option of the three that removes the crash mechanism entirely, since no non-migration-job container would ever call alembic again. (2) Wrap the existing per-service `alembic upgrade head` calls in a `pg_advisory_lock` so concurrent boots serialize instead of racing — this only fixes the concurrent-DDL race (D-02), not the stale-image-can't-resolve-a-future-revision crash, because the stale image still lacks the migration file needed to advance past its own local head. (3) Have entrypoint.sh catch the specific 'Can't locate revision' failure and, instead of exiting non-zero into a crash-restart loop, exit 0 / skip straight to running the task — treats the symptom (crash-looping) without removing the several-minute window where that resource is silently not running its workload. CI check to make the chosen fix verifiable either way: assert that `grep -c 'alembic upgrade head' entrypoint.sh` invocations reachable from more than one Railway resource's boot path is reduced to the intended count for whichever option is chosen, and add an integration test that boots two containers pointed at the same fresh Postgres from two different git revisions (one before, one after a migration) and asserts the older one either waits/no-ops or fails a documented, non-crash-looping way.

def run_migrations_online() -> None:
    connectable = create_engine(settings.sync_database_url)
    with connectable.connect() as connection:
        context.configure(connection=connection, target_metadata=target_metadata)
        with context.begin_transaction():
            context.run_migrations()
findings.failure_scenario: No advisory lock, `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, or any other mutual-exclusion mechanism appears anywhere in this file, entrypoint.sh, or alembic.ini (traced: grepped the whole repo for `advisory_lock`, `pg_advisory`, `FOR UPDATE`, `transaction_per_migration` — zero matches). Given that a push redeploys up to 9 resources near-simultaneously and each independently executes this exact function, it is possible for two or more containers to start `alembic upgrade head` while both still read the SAME pre-migration alembic_version row. What Postgres/Alembic then do (inferred from documented Postgres DDL-locking semantics, not executed against this repo's DB): the DDL statements in the migration (CREATE TABLE, ALTER TYPE, CREATE INDEX, ALTER COLUMN TYPE all take ACCESS EXCLUSIVE or SHARE locks) cause the second transaction to block behind the first's lock; once the first commits, the second's own attempt to run the identical DDL against now-already-migrated objects typically errors (e.g. 'relation already exists' for CREATE TABLE) rather than silently no-op'ing, because none of these migrations use IF NOT EXISTS guards except the enum ADD VALUE statements. A container that errors here exits non-zero into the same crash-restart loop as D-01, for a different underlying reason (a true race, not staleness).

gate.assert: Integration test: spin up two `alembic upgrade head` processes concurrently (e.g. via subprocess) against the same freshly-seeded test Postgres, both starting from the same revision, and assert the outcome is either (a) both succeed because a lock serialized them, or (b) the loser fails in a detected, logged, non-silent way — not a bare non-zero process exit indistinguishable from any other crash. Today this test does not exist (tests/conftest.py and tests/test_agent_job_cycle.py were the only test infra read; neither touches migrations).

findings.confidence: traced for absence of locking code; inferred for the specific concurrent-DDL outcome (not reproduced against a live DB in this task)

findings.failure_scenario: Neither `create_index` call passes `postgresql_concurrently=True`. Postgres takes a SHARE lock for the duration of a non-concurrent CREATE INDEX, which blocks INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (but not SELECT) on `entities` for the build duration. At the time this migration shipped, `entities` held on the order of 1,825-3,173 rows (docs/HANDOFF.md:39, docs/REMEDIATION_PLAN.md:3-4) — small enough that the actual 2026-07-30 lock window was almost certainly sub-second. The pattern is still flagged because (a) `entities` is written by every agent-jobs run (every 10 minutes) and by every cadence-scan tick, so ANY writer-blocking window on it, however brief, has live contenders; and (b) as the table grows, the same non-concurrent pattern on a future migration would scale its lock duration with table size, and CONCURRENTLY cannot be added retroactively to an already-shipped migration.

gate.assert: Add a lint/CI check that scans alembic/versions/*.py for `op.create_index(` calls lacking `postgresql_concurrently=True`, and fails the build unless the index target is a table created in the same migration (which is safe, since it is necessarily empty). Project CLAUDE.md-equivalent for this repo notes CI does not currently cover lint or boundary rules (docs/DECISIONS-PENDING.md:46-47: 'Nothing runs this gate but a person. There is no .github/workflows in the repo.') — traced: `find .. -maxdepth 1 -iname .github` returned nothing for this repo root.

findings.failure_scenario: `context.run_migrations()` applies EVERY pending revision between a container's current DB-recorded revision and head inside this single `begin_transaction()` block (alembic.ini has no `transaction_per_migration` override — traced, key absent from sourcing/alembic.ini). For a container that boots at head this is a no-op. But for any resource that has been down or unscheduled across more than one migration (e.g., a rarely-firing cron job like cadence-weekly, or a resource that was manually stopped), a single boot would run several migrations' DDL back-to-back in one transaction, meaning every ACCESS EXCLUSIVE/SHARE lock taken by an early migration in that batch (e.g. 006's CREATE INDEX on `entities`) is held until the LAST migration in the batch also commits — not released between migrations. This compounds D-03's lock-duration concern in the one scenario where table size and batch length both grow.

gate.assert: Before deploying a migration, check each of the 9 resources' currently-recorded alembic revision (e.g. via a one-off `SELECT version_num FROM alembic_version` — there is only one alembic_version row since all 9 resources share one DB, so this check is actually trivial: there is never more than one revision gap to worry about across resources, only across time if a resource has been offline). This finding is lower-severity than initially scoped for that reason: because all resources share ONE Postgres and hence one alembic_version row, in the common case every resource is either already at head or exactly one migration behind, not several — the multi-migration-batch scenario requires a resource to have missed more than one deploy's migrations while never restarting in between, which is uncommon for cron jobs firing every 10-15 minutes but plausible for cadence-weekly (7-day gaps) or morning-digest (skips weekends).

findings.failure_scenario: Three separate Railway cron-job resources — cadence-hourly, cadence-6h, cadence-weekly — all run TASK_MODE=cadence-scan (the same code path, entrypoint.sh:27-29) and are distinguished ONLY by a CADENCE_BUCKET env var each is presumably configured with individually (not verified — reading actual per-resource env values was avoided; see open_questions). If any one of the three is deployed/reconfigured without CADENCE_BUCKET set, `cadence_bucket` resolves to `None`, and app/pipeline/orchestrator.py:64 `if cadence_bucket: stmt = stmt.where(Source.cadence_bucket == cadence_bucket)` SKIPS the bucket filter entirely — the job silently scans ALL due sources across every bucket instead of just its own, with no error, no warning beyond a structured log line (cadence_scan.py:17 `logger.info("cadence_scan_starting", cadence_bucket=cadence_bucket, ...)` which logs `cadence_bucket=None` but nothing alerts on that). This both defeats the purpose of having three separate cadence tiers (rate-limiting/spreading load across sources per docs/HANDOFF.md's fetch-concurrency concerns) and could cause duplicate/overlapping scans of the same sources from multiple cron jobs within the same window.

gate.assert: Add a unit test asserting `run_due_scan(cadence_bucket=None)` is never reachable from a TASK_MODE=cadence-scan boot — either make CADENCE_BUCKET a required setting (fail entrypoint.sh fast, before calling the task, when TASK_MODE=cadence-scan and CADENCE_BUCKET is unset) or add an explicit `if cadence_bucket is None: raise` at the top of run_cadence_scan if 'scan everything' is never an intended production mode. If unscoped scanning IS an intended manual/ad-hoc mode, document it in .env.example and cadence_scan.py's docstring rather than leaving it as an undocumented fallthrough of a falsy check.

open_questions.question: How should migrations-on-boot be fixed, given D-01/D-02 share one root cause (every one of 9 resources unconditionally re-runs `alembic upgrade head` on every boot, with no locking)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the single change that would eliminate the largest number of findings at once (D-01, D-02, and D-04 all trace to entrypoint.sh:10/47 + alembic/env.py's transaction model).

options.option: Single dedicated one-shot migration job/phase; all 9 resources wait on it before starting their own boot logic
options.evidence_for: Structurally removes the crash mechanism entirely — no non-migration container would ever call alembic again, so 'old image vs new DB revision' becomes impossible.
options.evidence_against_or_cost: Not supported by anything observed in this repo today: railway.toml (sourcing/railway.toml:1-11) has no pre-deploy/release-phase field, and entrypoint.sh has no leader-election. Would require new Railway-level orchestration not present in this corpus.

options.option: Wrap the existing per-resource `alembic upgrade head` calls in a Postgres advisory lock
options.evidence_for: Smaller change; fixes D-02's concurrent-DDL race directly.
options.evidence_against_or_cost: Does not fix D-01's actual observed failure mode (a stale image's own alembic/versions/ directory lacks the new revision file entirely — no amount of lock-waiting lets it resolve a revision it doesn't have on disk).

options.option: Keep current per-resource migration calls, but make the crash path graceful (catch 'Can't locate revision', skip to running the task instead of exiting non-zero)
options.evidence_for: Smallest change; stops the crash-restart loop.
options.evidence_against_or_cost: Treats the symptom, not the cause — that resource still silently doesn't apply/benefit from the new migration and runs stale code against a schema the DB has already moved past, for the rest of the rollover window.
